text:
Dr Jones
Newton Memory Clinic
400 Rail Rd
Newtown

19/04/2015

Dear Dr Jones,
Re: Mrs. Patricia Welshman, DOB: 28/03/1930

Thank you for seeing Mrs. Welshman, an 85-year-old widow whose features are suggestive of
Alzheimer's disease. Your further assessment would be highly appreciated.

Although Mrs. Welshman is a mother of five children, she lives alone. Her past medical history
is unremarkable except for osteoporosis and hyperlipidemia for which, she is on osteo-vitamin
D, atorvastatin, ibuprofen, metoprolol and paracetamol. She has a strong family history of
Alzheimer's disease.

On 14/12/2014, Mrs. Welshman came for a regular check-up. At that time, her blood pressure
and LDL level were high but her vitamin D level was slightly low. Apart from that, her
medication scripts were spare; however, she claimed that she took her medications regularly.
Two months later, her condition had deteriorated as her LDL level had increased and her
vitamin D level had decreased significantly. Thus, she agreed to use a Webster pack.

Today, Mrs. Welshman was brought by her daughter complaining of poor memory, behavioral
changes as well as decision–making issues. Consequently, mini memory assessment was done
which revealed poor short-term memory.

Given the previous data, I would probably suspect that Mrs. Welshman might have Alzheimer's
disease. Therefore, your further assessment would be greatly valued. If you have any queries,
please contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
